symptom: An `exec` / `check --references` error on a CREATE WORKFLOW statement ends with 'hint: M.W is defined later in this script — move its create statement before this one', naming the failing workflow itself (or a workflow already created earlier in the script).
cause: annotateForwardRef draws candidate names from scriptContext.allNames (which includes workflows) and excludes the statement's own name and already-created names via scriptContext.has — which checked modules, entities, enumerations, microflows, nanoflows, pages, snippets and code actions but NOT workflows. A parallel list that drifted from the one it filters.
insight: Two lists over the same kinds (allNames and has) with nothing tying them together — the same drift shape as collectDefinitions/collectSingle. The misfire only became visible once an error routinely named its own workflow, i.e. a new rule surfaced a latent bug in how every rule's message is decorated. When adding a document kind to scriptContext, check every method that enumerates kinds, not just the collector.
